channel.title: Loadout Rank: new AI releases
channel.description: Notable AI tool and model releases, each linked to its primary source.

item.title: Google DeepMind: Gemini 4 Carbon: Google's new frontier model, led by cybersecurity and long tasks (limited access)
item.description: Google's next frontier Gemini model is built for long-horizon work and cybersecurity, and Google says it can work through complex coding tasks for days without getting stuck or taking shortcuts. Google-reported: #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 with a score of 59, 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8% on ExploitGym, 71.0% on CWE-bench, and #4 on WebDev Arena (1768). Access is limited for now: a subset of cyber defenders gets it first this week, then trusted partners through Google's Fairwind Program, with developer, business and consumer access coming soon. Introductory API pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output (cached input 95% off), rising later to $4 and $20. Benchmarks are Google's own.

item.title: GitHub: Copilot Fusion: Copilot now orchestrates several models per task (GA)
item.description: GitHub Copilot can now route and combine models from different labs on a single task instead of using one model at a time. Pick an effort level (Standard, High or Max) and Fusion picks the models and a workflow: Single, Cascade (escalate when needed) or Critique (one model checks another). GitHub-reported: Fusion Max scored 60 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max, at about half the API cost per task, about half the tokens and roughly 40% less time. Usage is billed at each underlying model's standard rate, with 30% off on paid plans through Nov. 30. Generally available on all Copilot plans in VS Code, the Copilot app, Copilot CLI and JetBrains IDEs; admins choose which models it may use. Figures are GitHub's own.

item.title: GitHub: Replica: open-source AI prototyping with your own design system (MIT)
item.description: GitHub's design team open-sourced the tool it uses to build interactive prototypes from plain-language prompts, using your team's real design system and components instead of generic UI. You drive it from the GitHub Copilot app, and an optional self-hosted Replica Hub lets teammates view prototypes and leave comments. Free and open source under the MIT license on GitHub. Handy for quickly mocking up a game launcher, mod manager or dashboard that actually looks like your product.

item.title: Particle: Particle-1: a token-efficient coding model built on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
item.description: The first model from Particle, a new company from Mixpanel founder Suhail Doshi, is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash post-trained with reinforcement learning to finish software and data-engineering tasks with far fewer tokens. Particle-reported: about 45% fewer tokens on average, 28.4% to 52.2% fewer output tokens and 34.4% to 51.6% lower cost per task than the base model on DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1, ReactBench and ADE Bench, with pass rates within the base model's confidence intervals and general benchmarks like GPQA Diamond close to the base. Fewer tokens also means tasks finish sooner. Available now through Particle's own inference API, which Particle says is also partnered with OpenRouter. Benchmarks are Particle's own.

item.title: SenseTime: SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video: an open model that makes videos by writing code (Apache 2.0)
item.description: SenseTime released a lightweight open model that turns a text idea into executable code, which then renders a short video, so every shot stays editable as code you can tweak with follow-up requests. It can also recreate and remix reference videos in code. SenseTime open-sourced the weights plus a Skill for coding agents, along with the prompts and full generation runs behind every showcase video, each made from a single prompt in one run. The 27B model is fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B with a 512K-token context and is meant to be driven from an agent harness (SenseTime recommends Claude Code). Weights on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0; at 27B you'll want a strong GPU or a hosted endpoint.

item.title: Simulon: Simulon Reality-Aware Rendering: AI characters that react to your real-world scene (iPhone)
item.description: Simulon's phone app now lets you place AI-generated neural assets (creatures, characters, objects) into the real world, act out a scene, and get back a rendered take where those assets respond to what you do, what you say and the room around you. When you stop recording, Simulon regenerates the final video from your recording as a new performance of the scene rather than an overlay on the footage. Available now on iPhone, with Android coming soon; the app is free to try with 100 one-time starter credits, and Simulon Plus is $14.99 a month and Pro $39.99 a month. A fun one for creators making short films, skits or game-style clips.

item.title: Articul8: Bivia: a multimodal model that returns decisions, not text (API)
item.description: Articul8 (an Intel spinout) launched a compact decision model for agents: give it an input such as text, images, documents, code, signals, audio or video plus a question, and it returns a typed decision (choice, yes/no, score, extraction and more) with a calibrated confidence instead of generating a chat reply. It can abstain and flag calls it isn't sure about, has Fast and Deep modes, and works in 50+ languages, per Articul8. Because it generates no output tokens, Articul8 says you pay only for input tokens, which suits high-volume routing and triage steps inside an agent. Available via API now; the first 10,000 users get up to 1 billion free tokens with no subscription.

item.title: OpenBMB: MiniCPM-OCR 1.0: a 1.3B open OCR model that runs on phones and laptops (Apache 2.0)
item.description: OpenBMB released a small open model for reading real-world documents (text, tables, formulas, charts, seals and key fields) from scans, photos, curved or skewed pages and PDFs, in Chinese and English. OpenBMB-reported: 93.68 on Real5-OmniDocBench with leading results on OmniDocBench v1.6, Wild-OmniDocBench and olmOCR-Bench, and about 1.49x the throughput of PaddleOCR-VL-1.6. A companion 2B model, MiniCPM-OCR Jev, scores OCR results so you can flag likely errors for human review, and it can check other OCR models' output too. Day-one support for vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp and Ollama, with quantized builds and an Apple silicon port; weights on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0, plus a free API. Benchmarks are OpenBMB's own.

item.title: Google DeepMind: Genie 4: real-time interactive world model with native audio (research preview)
item.description: DeepMind's new world model generates explorable worlds you move through in real time with standard keyboard controls, and now generates the sound with them: music, ambient noise and dialogue from the people in the scene. You can steer a running simulation in plain language, like changing the weather, moving the camera or adding a person or object, and Gemini adapts the prompt to the scene and keeps the world coherent between your inputs. DeepMind says it builds on Gemini Omni for real-world appearance and behavior, with better photorealism, physics (aerodynamics, collisions) and much more natural human characters than Genie 3. Rolling out first as a research preview for trusted testers; Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio come next, with a waitlist open now. A big one for anyone prototyping game worlds.

item.title: Liquid AI: LFM3: six open-weight ~2B models for text, vision, audio and omni
item.description: Liquid AI's new generation of small on-device models: text, vision (now with video input), audio (speech in and out, 18 languages), an omni model that sees, listens and talks, and two decision models (d1-2B, d1-Omni-2B), all branched from one LFM3-1.7B-Base backbone pretrained on 22T tokens with a new tri-hybrid architecture. Liquid AI-reported: LFM3-1.7B beats its own LFM2.5-2.6B with 35% fewer parameters, the text model fits in about 1 GB at 4-bit with a 256K-token context, and it's post-trained to run in agent harnesses such as Hermes Agent, Pi and OpenClaw. Every model can be fine-tuned on a single GPU. Weights on Hugging Face under Liquid's LFM Open License v1.0 (not Apache or MIT), plus Liquid's API and Playground; runs in llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM and SGLang, with day-0 partners including OpenRouter and Vercel, and it's on Ollama. Benchmarks are Liquid AI's own.

item.title: inclusionAI (Ant Group): Ling-3.1-flash-1019 (open weights, MIT)
item.description: An upgraded post-training of Ant Group's Ling-3.1-flash: a 560B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 25B active per token and a 1M-token context window, aimed at reasoning and multi-step agent work. Lab-reported gains over Ling-3.1-flash: AA-Briefcase about 1400 to 1524 Elo, AutomationBench-AA 62% to 68%, CritPt 18% to 26% and SciCode 54% to 57%, for a score of 44 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 (up from 41). Ant also released Ling-3.1-flash-base as an open foundation for further training. Weights on Hugging Face under MIT; at this size it's a server/cloud model, not a laptop one. Benchmarks are inclusionAI's own.

item.title: DiffuSpace: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview: open diffusion language model (Apache 2.0)
item.description: From the team behind HKU's Dream 7B: a 35B mixture-of-experts language model (about 3B active) that writes by filling in blocks of tokens in parallel instead of one token at a time, built from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, with a thinking mode. DiffuSpace-reported: SWE-bench Verified 73.6, Terminal-Bench 2.1 51.7 and τ³ 65.3, ahead of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and diffusion rivals in its tables, and about 680 tokens/s on one NVIDIA GB300 (BF16, batch size 1, internal agent workloads) or 515 tokens/s on an H200. Weights under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face, ModelScope and GitHub; the lab lists SGLang and llama.cpp support, but the full BF16 weights need a large data-center GPU, so it's not a typical local pick yet. A decision model built on it is coming later. Benchmarks are DiffuSpace's own.

item.title: Replit: Cloud Agents for existing company codebases
item.description: Anyone on a team (designers, PMs, support leads) can describe a change to the company's real app in plain language; Replit's Cloud Agents find the code, make the change with a live preview, click through it in an isolated cloud sandbox, fix what fails, and open a GitHub pull request or GitLab merge request with screenshots and video of it working. Engineers still review and approve what ships, and when review feedback is worth keeping the agent proposes updates to the team's agent skills (that part is early access). An admin sets up one shared environment from your repos that stays synced to main. You can also start requests by mentioning @Replit in Slack, with Microsoft Teams support coming. Available to all Replit Pro and Enterprise customers.

item.title: Baidu: Unlimited OCR 2: open document-parsing model for very long documents (MIT)
item.description: Baidu's second Unlimited OCR model reads whole multi-page documents in one request, using cross-page context, and keeps decoding speed and memory nearly constant no matter how long the document gets, thanks to a new attention design (SR-SWA) that compresses the text-to-image interactions into a fixed set of working references. Baidu reports state-of-the-art results on long-document parsing benchmarks, including MarathonDocBench, a new hundred-page benchmark it released alongside. Weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope under MIT, with Transformers and SGLang support, a free Hugging Face demo, and availability on Baidu Cloud. Benchmarks are Baidu's own.

item.title: Opera: WebAI: local AI models built into the Opera browser (early preview)
item.description: Opera One now ships local AI that websites and browser extensions can use through WebAI, a proposed web standard Opera says is backed by companies such as Google and Microsoft: text generation, content classification and finding how pieces of information relate, all running on your own computer with no AI subscription, per-request fee or data sent to an AI service. At launch it uses Google's Gemma and, on Macs, Apple's on-device foundation model; Opera says the design is model-agnostic and built around open models. Opt-in: nothing downloads until you turn it on, and each site needs permission. Early preview on 64-bit Windows PCs (Intel or AMD) and Apple silicon Macs; speed depends on your hardware. Opera GX (its gaming browser) and Opera Neon get it later. Opera also launched HTML-in-Canvas, which puts live, clickable web pages inside 2D and 3D scenes, with game-style demos aimed at Opera GX.

item.title: Entire: Entire: a Git forge built for agents and humans working together
item.description: Former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke's company launched a full Git host where agents are first-class collaborators. Trails replace pull requests: every push is scored by agent-run evaluations so you see what changed and whether it works. Entire says pushes are up to 89x faster than GitHub on its new Git-compatible backend (EntireDB), and its Continuous Memory pairs a codebase graph (up to 71% token savings, per Entire) with an agent brain built from previous sessions and prompts. Teams can move off GitHub Actions to Buildkite or Depot CI, and all Trails data is also available through the open-source Entire CLI so coding agents can fix findings in a loop. Speed and savings figures are Entire's own.

item.title: OpenAI: GPT-6.1 Terra (fast, low-cost computer-use model)
item.description: OpenAI's new mid-tier model for everyday computer work: reading screens, filling out forms, interpreting technical drawings, editing video and writing, plus everyday agentic coding. OpenAI-reported: on its Agents' Last Exam computer-use benchmark it scores 15 points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra at medium effort for about a third of the cost and is on par with GPT-6 Astra at a tenth of the per-token price; Terminal-Bench 4.0 50.3% at max effort (GPT-5.6 Terra 21.5%); error rate on its hallucination-inducing prompts down from 53.6% to 16.7% at low effort. OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra remain better for the hardest coding. Available now to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and in the API as gpt-6.1-terra at $1 / $5 per million input / output tokens ($0.05 cached input). Also GA in GitHub Copilot (Pro and up), Amazon Bedrock (up to 1M input tokens) and Microsoft Foundry. Benchmarks are OpenAI's own.

item.title: Mirendil: Fern 0.1: 10M-token-context model (early access)
item.description: The first model from Mirendil, pretrained from scratch with a context window of up to 10 million tokens, which Mirendil says is about half a million lines of code, dozens to hundreds of full agent traces, or days of an agent's work held in context at once. Fern 0.1 is Mirendil's base model after a short round of post-training, aimed at high-volume agentic work for people building AI: agentic coding across large repos, debugging training runs from logs, reading agent traces end to end and auditing training data. Mirendil says new versions will ship frequently and fuller long-context results are coming. Hosted early access by request only; no open weights, pricing or public API yet. Results are the company's own.

item.title: Runway: App Studio: build your own creative AI apps by describing them
item.description: Describe the tool you want in plain language and Runway builds, tests, deploys and hosts a custom app with its own interface that generates images, video and audio with Runway's models, your Brand Kits, Workflows, assets and references. No code, API keys or hosting setup; you can refine it in chat, preview changes, roll back versions and inspect the code. Launches with built-in apps you can use or remix, including Character Swap, AutoComp (product swaps in footage), Product Portfolio, 3D Camera Control and Precise Edit; the old Runway Apps now live here. Share with your team or publish a link anyone with a Runway account can use (visitors pay for their own generations). Included in every paid plan and billed from your existing Runway credits.

item.title: Nanbeige Lab: Nanbeige4.3-33B (open weights, Apache 2.0)
item.description: Nanbeige Lab (part of BOSS Zhipin's parent Kanzhun) released a 33B dense model aimed at agentic coding and terminal work, with a 512K-token (524,288) context and a chat template that can switch thinking on or off and keep earlier reasoning across turns. Lab-reported versus Qwen3.8-27B: Terminal-Bench 2.1 80.9 vs 73.0 and DeepSWE 65.5 vs 42.5, but SWE-Bench Pro 60.3 vs 61.7 and GDPval 84.8 vs 86.4, so it isn't ahead everywhere. BF16 weights plus a Base model on Hugging Face, running with Transformers, SGLang or vLLM; Nanbeige says it is the teacher for an upcoming Nanbeige4.3-3B. Scores are the lab's own and not independently checked.

item.title: Ollama: Speech models in Ollama (local text-to-speech with Phonon)
item.description: Ollama can now turn text into speech on your own machine, starting with Gradium's small Phonon models: ollama run phonon "Hello" speaks out loud, a chat model's reply can be piped into it so it starts talking after the first sentence, output can be saved as a WAV file, and the OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech endpoint streams audio so existing OpenAI SDK code only needs a new base URL. English phonon is Apache 2.0; the French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and multilingual 40M models are CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial). macOS on Apple Silicon only for now (Ollama 0.40.11 or later), with Windows and Linux coming soon; Ollama reports it ran 35% faster than Gradium's own runtime on an M5 Max MacBook Pro.

item.title: Anthropic: MCP Tasks and Elicitations in Claude Code (public beta)
item.description: Claude Code now supports two MCP extensions that plugin and MCP-server builders can use today. Tasks let a server run a long job (deep research, a report export, a build) on its own: Claude's tool call returns as soon as the server accepts the job, Claude keeps working, and the result comes back when the job ends; running tasks show up in /tasks, where you can stop them, and a task on a remote server keeps running after you exit and can be picked up again by resuming the session. Elicitations let a server pause mid-task to ask you for input, such as confirming a refund or filling in a missing detail. Public beta in the Claude Code CLI v2.1.304 or later (terminal sessions, Agent SDK sessions and GitHub Actions runs); not yet in the VS Code extension or desktop app, and not on third-party providers such as Amazon Bedrock. Anthropic says more Claude products are coming soon.

item.title: Moonshot AI: Kimi K3.1 Pro + K3.1 Pro Highspeed (open weights due by Nov 4)
item.description: Moonshot's new flagship is a further post-trained Kimi K3: a 2.8T-total / 104B-active multimodal mixture-of-experts model with a 1M-token context, plus a Highspeed variant Moonshot says runs 2–3× faster. Pitched at long-horizon coding (including full game projects in Unity, Unreal Engine and Godot), parametric 3D modeling by scripting Blender and CAD tools, and finance work. Lab-reported: Terminal-Bench 4.0 65.7% (Claude Opus 5.5 66.4%, GPT-6 Astra 58.2%), and on Moonshot's internal hallucination stress test the claim-level error rate fell from 23.4% (K3) to 8.3%. Moonshot says it removed cyber-related training data for the open-weight release. Live now on Kimi.ai and the Kimi apps, Kimi Work (3.1.0+), Kimi Code (/model) and the Kimi API (kimi-k3.1-pro, kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed); full weights due by Nov 4, 2026. Benchmarks are Moonshot's own.

item.title: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB (open small model for local agents)
item.description: The 4GB Bolt promised with Nemotron 3.5 has shipped: an 8B (4B effective) model post-trained by NVIDIA from Gemma 4 E4B for voice and device assistants, in-game NPCs and robot interfaces running locally on GeForce RTX, Jetson, RTX Spark and DGX Spark. Multi-turn tool calling, a conversational mode for short speech-ready replies, reasoning you can switch on or off, 64K context and 35 languages; ships as a ~4GB Q4_K_M build plus BF16 and a DFlash speculative-decoding drafter. NVIDIA reports ~40% higher average scores than its Nemotron 3 Nano 4B on its conversational-agent benchmark set and up to ~80% fewer output tokens than peers with reasoning on. Open weights on Hugging Face under OpenMDW-1.1. Benchmarks are NVIDIA's own.

item.title: MiniMax: MiniMax M3.1 Flash open weights (MiniMax Community License)
item.description: The weights MiniMax promised at launch are now on Hugging Face: about 428B total / 23B active parameters, text, image and video in, up to 1M-token context, with the DSpark speculative-decoding draft head included and SGLang, vLLM and TokenSpeed as the recommended servers. Not an OSI license: non-commercial use is free; commercial use requires displaying "Built with MiniMax M3.1-Flash" and a one-time notice to MiniMax, and products with more than $20M in yearly revenue need MiniMax's prior written authorization. Together AI, Fireworks, Modular and DigitalOcean offered hosted versions on day one.

item.title: Cursor: Computer Use: agents drive desktop apps
item.description: Cursor's agents can now control a computer, clicking and typing in desktop apps such as the iOS Simulator to test the features they build. For self-hosted workers it is an explicit opt-in on macOS and Linux (agent worker --computer-use start); macOS needs Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions for the Cursor Computer Use helper, and Linux workers can also share the agent's desktop so teammates can watch or take control.

item.title: Abacus.AI: Smaug-Nemotron-3.5 (agentic coding fine-tune, open weights)
item.description: Abacus.AI's supervised fine-tune of NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (120B total / 12B active hybrid Mamba-2 + MoE + attention, text, image and video in, up to 1M-token context) on filtered multi-turn, tool-using coding trajectories. The architecture is unchanged, so it's a drop-in replacement wherever the base model runs. Abacus reports gains in agentic coding over the base (Terminal-Bench 2.1 69.1 vs 60.7, SWE-bench Verified 72.3 vs 71.1, DeepSWE 27.4 vs 24.7) with reasoning, coding and vision scores at parity. BF16 weights plus an NVFP4 build on Hugging Face under the OpenMDW 1.1 license inherited from the base. Announced Oct 23 by Abacus CEO Bindu Reddy; the Hugging Face repo was created Oct 18. Benchmarks are Abacus's own.

item.title: Canva: Canva Craft image model
item.description: Canva's first in-house image model, trained from scratch by Canva Research for design work: it plans the composition (elements, layout, scale and any text) before rendering, at up to 2K resolution in 30+ aspect ratios, with text in 55 languages, and its outputs convert into editable layers with Magic Layers. Available to all Canva users globally via Dream Lab and to developers through Canva's public API; Canva MCP support is coming soon. Canva cites a #4 debut on the DesignArena image leaderboard.

item.title: Ideogram: Ideogram Vector 1.0 (text or image to editable SVG)
item.description: Ideogram's first vector model generates clean, editable SVGs with smooth gradients and sharp typography from a prompt, or converts an existing image into a scalable vector, for logos, print and merch, labels and illustrations. Live in Ideogram and the API, where text-to-vector costs $0.13 / $0.16 / $0.20 per SVG at low / medium / high quality ($0.32 for high with references) and image-to-vector costs $0.10 per image.

item.title: OpenAI: Decisions API generally available (GPT-6 Luna)
item.description: A dedicated endpoint for the small, bounded calls apps and agents make all day: ask up to 400 questions per request about text, images or JSON and get back typed answers instead of generated text: a probability that a condition is true (predicate), one option from a fixed list (choice), or a rubric score. OpenAI says it is up to 10x faster than asking GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API. New since the Oct 6 beta: prompt caching, JSON input, images inside individual questions, US/EU regional processing and a native GPT-Live integration (for example, picking an avatar's reaction while someone talks). $0.10 per 1M input tokens, $0.01 cached, and no output-token charges.

item.title: Hugging Face: Carbon-X: open model you can chat with about DNA (Apache 2.0)
item.description: A 14.8B dense model built from Qwen3-14B and trained jointly on DNA and text, with a 40,960-token context: paste a sequence and ask whether a mutation looks benign or pathogenic, which regions control gene activity, which organism group it comes from, or have it continue or write sequences, with explanations. Hugging Face reports a 66.7% average across five DNA benchmarks, close to GPT-6.1 Sol's 67.5%. Weights fit on one 80GB GPU in bfloat16 (GGUF builds too), so sensitive sequences can stay on your own hardware. Built with Zhongguancun Academy, TIGEM and the University of Naples Federico II. Not clinically validated and not for medical decisions; benchmarks are Hugging Face's own.

item.title: KRAFTON: Raon-1 mini preview (open weights, Apache 2.0)
item.description: The PUBG publisher's AI lab trained this open language model from scratch: a 28.8B-total / 4.3B-active mixture-of-experts model with KRAFTON's own linear-attention design and a 262,144-token context, strongest at Korean conversation, instruction following and agent tool calling (works with Hermes Agent, Pi and OpenCode). KRAFTON reports SWE-bench Verified 70.8, GPQA Diamond 84.3 and AIME 2026 93.3. Trained on seven languages. An NVFP4 build runs on a single RTX 5090 (32GB), with MXFP8, GGUF and MLX builds plus a DFlash2 draft model for faster decoding. Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face (access request with automatic approval) and a free playground for a limited time. A preview: specs may change before the final release and technical report. Benchmarks are KRAFTON's own.

item.title: Anthropic: Claude Duet (proactive agent app, research preview)
item.description: A new standalone app where Claude works as a proactive agent: a short morning brief across your connected apps, check-ins every few hours to flag what needs you, and background tasks (scheduling, dashboards, forecasts, prototypes and web apps) that keep running on its own virtual machine with a browser after you close your laptop or phone. Built around Claude Opus 5.5 and carries over your Claude memory, skills and connectors. It shows you exactly what it's about to do and waits for approval before sending a message, making a payment, signing a document or deleting anything; some actions, like trading securities, are off-limits. Research preview by waitlist for US Pro and Max subscribers on iOS, Android and claude.ai, sharing your plan's usage limits.

item.title: Recursive: Flint (open-weight local coding model, Apache 2.0)
item.description: Recursive's first model: a 40B-total / ~2.5B-active mixture-of-experts model built for fast agentic coding on local hardware, which Recursive says a small team of people and agents built from scratch in under four months with its automated research system. Lab-reported scores: Terminal-Bench 2.1 54.9%, SWE-bench Pro v2 89.7%, SWE-bench Verified 74.2%. Recursive reports 125+ tokens/s on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro and 150+ tokens/s on a 64GB NVIDIA RTX Spark at short contexts. Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face; works with llama.cpp, Ollama, Unsloth, LM Studio, vLLM and SGLang, plus Recursive's own rec engine for M4 Pro and M5 Pro/Max Macs. Benchmarks are Recursive's own.

item.title: Anthropic: Claude Security continuous scanning (public beta)
item.description: Claude Security now keeps watching connected repositories instead of waiting for someone to start a scan: after connecting through the Claude GitHub app it re-checks code as it changes, marks findings fixed when the fix lands (whether fixed in Claude Code or elsewhere) and reopens them automatically if the issue returns. Each project gets a knowledge base for your environment's controls, and it connects to other tools through an API and MCP. Public beta for Claude Enterprise customers, with $25,000 in free usage credits per month for two months (usage through Dec 31, 2026).

item.title: Base Labs (Baseten): mammoth-1 and elephant-1 decision models (open weights, MIT)
item.description: Two decision models post-trained from Qwen3.5: give them a state and a set of questions and they return a calibrated probability for every option in a single pass, for routing, classification, safety checks and scoring rather than chat. mammoth-1 (27B) scores 71.24 on the Jev Decision Index 0.4 (#1 of 208 models by Base Labs' count); elephant-1 (9B) scores 62.65, the best under 15B. MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face that self-host on one CUDA GPU; Baseten offered both free on its Model APIs through Oct 27, 2026. Benchmarks are Base Labs' own.

item.title: Cursor: Agent SDK: build, test and deploy agents as code (GA)
item.description: The framework Cursor uses for its own managed agents (Bugbot, Security Reviewer, Rollouts) is now generally available. An agent is a small project: the prompt is Markdown, each tool is a TypeScript function, and skills, MCP connections and channels sit in their own folders, so changes go through normal code review. Agents can wake on pull request, comment and CI events from GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket, Slack mentions and DMs, webhooks or a cron schedule, and can hand work to subagents. Built-in evals and pull-request replay test behavior before shipping; deploy to Cursor's hosted infrastructure with one command or run it yourself as a single Node process. Starter templates include a security reviewer, a PR autofixer and a Linear or Jira triager. Cursor dated the launch Oct 20 and promoted it on X on Oct 26.

item.title: iFLYTEK: Spark-X2.6-4B (open on-device agent model, Apache 2.0)
item.description: iFLYTEK's SparkLLM team updated its 4B on-device model a little over a month after Spark-X2.5-4B: the architecture is unchanged and the gains come from post-training for coding, tool-using agents, long context and multilingual work, with three thinking levels (none, low, high) to trade quality for speed. iFLYTEK-reported (high thinking): BFCL-V4 71.8, MCP-Atlas 62.4, BrowseComp 53.1, SWE Pro 54.3, and it says the model matches or beats some ~9B models. Weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope (FP8, INT8 and GGUF builds too) and on Ollama (ollama run SparkLLM/Spark-X2.6-4B), with vLLM and SGLang guides. Scores are the company's own.

item.title: ElevenLabs: Eleven Realtime v1 Mini and v1 Max (speech-to-speech voice agents)
item.description: A new class of speech-to-speech models where each model is a complete voice agent, with no separate speech recognition, LLM and text-to-speech to wire together. Both handle 90+ languages and any of the 17,000+ voices in the ElevenLabs library. Mini is the low-cost pick for assistants, tutors and interactive characters; Max is for support, lead qualification and multi-step workflows with heavy tool calling. In Artificial Analysis evaluations cited by ElevenLabs: Big Bench Audio 98.8% (Max) / 75.9% (Mini), 0.57 s / 0.62 s average time to start speaking, Full-Duplex-Bench 94.1% / 95.8%, tool-use completion 87.1% / 60.3%. Available in ElevenAgents and through a Realtime API that follows OpenAI's Realtime spec (WebSocket only), so existing code needs only a new endpoint and model name.

item.title: Simular: Agent S4: computer-use agent that evolves its own tools (open source, Apache 2.0)
item.description: Simular's research release in its open-source Agent-S repo, with the paper Evolving Agent Interfaces. Instead of clicking through apps the way a person would, a Builder agent studies a computer-use agent's attempts and writes and revises a small Python tool library (a shadow interface) for it, and population-based evolution keeps the versions that score best on held-out tasks. Simular reports 21.3% on OSWorld V2, which scores strict pass/fail, with Qwen3.8-27B: 3.8x the same model with fixed interfaces and above its reported GPT-5.5 (13.0%) and Claude Opus 4.8 (20.6%) runs, at roughly 4.3% and 1.5% of their cost; on ScienceBoard, success rose from 41.4% to 58.6%. This is research code, not an app: runs need a clone of the repo, the OSWorld-V2 setup, AWS VMs and model credentials. Benchmarks are Simular's own.

item.title: Perplexity: Perplexity Computer runs fully local on Mac
item.description: The Perplexity Mac app can now run Computer's model, harness and task execution entirely on device, with planning, reasoning and file processing kept on the Mac and, with permission, work across local files and apps like Notes and Mail. Launches with Qwen 3.6 or PPLX Pro (Perplexity's post-trained Qwen) as local models; you can authorize escalation to the cloud for current information, browser use, connected apps or one of 15+ frontier models. For Pro, Max and Enterprise subscribers on supported Apple silicon Macs; 36GB or more of memory recommended. Hybrid Compute remains available.

item.title: Google: TorchTPU: native PyTorch on TPUs (open source, Apache 2.0)
item.description: Google's native PyTorch backend for Cloud TPUs, co-developed with Meta's PyTorch team and open-sourced at PyTorch Conference 2026: existing PyTorch code runs with minimal changes (.to("tpu")), with eager mode for debugging, torch.compile for production and native distributed APIs. Works with vLLM, SGLang, llm-d, TorchTitan, Ray, TorchRec and Hugging Face, and Google shipped new PyTorch-native vLLM and SGLang engines for TPU on top of it. Install with pip install torch_tpu; it replaces the now-deprecated PyTorch/XLA.

item.title: Eagle AI: EAGLE-4 speculative decoding (source-available)
item.description: The next version of the EAGLE speculative-decoding method: one trained drafter per target model adapts how much it drafts to the hardware and load, from a single request to hundreds at once and from GPUs down to CPUs and a phone. Eagle reports 647 tokens/s for one request (2.74× vanilla) and 33,480 aggregate tokens/s at 512 concurrent requests (1.69×) on NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with four B300 GPUs, plus day-0 results on AMD Instinct MI350X. Code and drafter checkpoints are public, but under the Eagle 4 Source-Available License, which is not open source; commercial use needs a license from Eagle. Benchmarks are Eagle's own.

item.title: Mistral: Voxtral 3 speech models + voice agent API
item.description: A new family of speech models plus a voice agent API that chains realtime transcription, a Mistral LLM for reasoning and tool calls, and speech output in one streaming pipeline; it can answer and place calls over SIP and run in browsers and apps over WebRTC. Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 handles 50+ languages with diarization and context biasing ($0.004/min); Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 is 4B parameters ($0.0035/min batch); Mini Transcribe Realtime 3 targets sub-500ms latency ($0.008/min); Voxtral Mini TTS 3 covers 35+ languages and 50+ dialects with emotion and pacing control ($13 per 1M characters). Voice agent API from $0.04/min with Mistral Small 4. Via Mistral's API or self-deployment; comparisons are Mistral's own.

item.title: Ornith: Ornith-1.5-122B (open weights, MIT)
item.description: A 122B mixture-of-experts reasoning model for coding and agent work that Ornith says serves on a single 80GB GPU; 262,144-token context, extendable to about 1M with YaRN. Lab-reported scores: SWE-bench Verified 84.5, Terminal-Bench 2.1 81.2, SWE-bench Pro 76.9. MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face in BF16 plus FP8, NVFP4, GGUF and MLX builds, and on Ollama (ollama run ornith-1.5:122b). Ornith-1.5 extends Ornith-1.0, which was built on Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4. Benchmarks are Ornith's own.

item.title: Bria: Fibo 2.0 (open weights, image generation + editing)
item.description: Bria's 8B-parameter model puts text-to-image and instruction-based image editing in one set of weights, with masked edits and up to 4 reference images, structured JSON (VGL) prompts and better text rendering. Two checkpoints: Fibo 2.0 Dev (full base for fine-tuning) and Edit Turbo (4-step editing). Bria cites #1 among open-weights models for image editing on Artificial Analysis as of Oct 20. Trained only on licensed data; weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (commercial use needs a Bria agreement); also on the Bria API, fal and ComfyUI nodes.

item.title: Hao AI Lab: FastH3 Omni (open-weight fast video + audio)
item.description: FastVideo (Hao AI Lab, UC San Diego) with Nuva Lab open-sourced a distilled MiniMax H3 model for reference-guided video with synchronized stereo audio: a prompt plus up to 9 images, 3 videos and 3 audio clips (12 references max) produces 5–15 second clips at 24 fps in eight transformer evaluations. FastVideo measured up to ~12× lower end-to-end latency than the base model on eight GB200 GPUs; NVFP4 weights and recipes target DGX Spark and RTX 5090, with a ComfyUI FP8 build. Weights use the MiniMax H3 community license.

item.title: Gradium: Phonon on-device text-to-speech (open weights)
item.description: Tiny streaming TTS models that run offline on phones, laptops, a Raspberry Pi 5 and inside a browser tab: Phonon 31m (English, 64.5 MB, Apache 2.0) and Phonon 40m in English, French, German, Spanish and Portuguese plus a multilingual model (CC BY-NC 4.0, gated). Rust runtime with Python, npm, Swift and Android bindings and an OpenAI-compatible speech server; Gradium says up to 22× faster than real time on an iPhone 16 Pro. Stable runtime v0.4.0 published Oct 20; Gradium's announcement post is dated Oct 21.

item.title: humans&: Ampersand v0.1 (collaborator model)
item.description: humans&'s first model is built to help groups of people pursue individual and shared goals over long periods, trained with reinforcement learning on long-horizon social simulations; it can choose to reply or stay silent in a group conversation. Built on GLM 5.3 (about 744B total / 40B active parameters, 1,048,576-token context), text only, API-only via the Agents API as ampersand-v0.1. humans& calls its evaluation results tentative.

item.title: Asymptote Labs: Beacon: shared memory for coding agents (open source, MIT)
item.description: Officially launched Oct 20 alongside a $5.5M seed round: Beacon captures session history across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Cline and 20+ other harnesses into local JSONL, then turns useful workflows, corrections and debugging patterns into reviewed knowledge that future agents retrieve through MCP or Agent Skills. Local-first; MIT-licensed on GitHub (repo public before the launch).

item.title: fal + Black Forest Labs: FLUX 3 Max video model (fast text and image to video)
item.description: fal Research post-trained Black Forest Labs' FLUX 3 video model for speed and quality: text-to-video and image-to-video at 720p, with a 10-second clip in about 12.45 seconds versus 126.44 for FLUX 3 and 277.80 for Seedance 2.5. It scores 1,139 Elo on Artificial Analysis's preliminary image-to-video arena, tied for #1 (MiniMax H3 is listed first at 1,141 within the margin). Only on fal's API, billed per second of output: $0.0425/s at 720p while 75% off until Nov 7, then $0.17/s list. Speed and Elo figures are as reported by fal.

item.title: Google: Gemini API CLI (gemini-api, experimental preview)
item.description: A zero-dependency command-line binary for macOS, Linux and Windows that puts the Gemini API in your terminal and in any coding agent with shell access (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity and others): run prompts, generate images, video, speech and music straight to disk, analyze PDFs, images and YouTube videos, transcribe audio to SRT, and start background Managed Agents such as Deep Research. Media commands print only the output file path, and every command describes itself offline (--help, --schema, --dry-run, JSON output with --jq) so agents stop guessing model IDs or dumping base64 into their context. Apache 2.0 on GitHub; needs a Gemini API key. Published Oct 19 (v0.4.3); Google's developer push on X came Oct 22.

item.title: Cloudflare: Clairic extraction model on Workers AI (preview)
item.description: Cloudflare's first System One extraction model (@cf/cloudflare/clairic): send text, plus up to four images, with a schema of typed fields and get one typed value per field (exact text spans with character offsets, numbers, dates, durations, lists, estimates with an 80% interval, and forecasts up to 64 steps), or null when the input doesn't determine it. Every answer carries a confidence score and p_null. Answers in one pass without generating tokens and charges only for input: $0.10 per 1M input tokens; 65,536-token context. Preview on Workers AI; Cloudflare says open weights are coming soon.

item.title: Inception: Mercury 3 (diffusion LLM)
item.description: Inception's largest diffusion language model, generating tokens in parallel rather than one at a time: Inception reports 1,068 tokens/s on NVIDIA GPUs and says it matches or beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on its benchmarks while running 4–8× faster. 1M-token context (up from 260K on Mercury 2.5). List price $0.20 / $0.70 per 1M input/output tokens, 50% off at launch ($0.10 / $0.35); cached input 90% off. OpenAI-compatible; on the Inception API, OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel, with 100M free tokens for new API keys. Benchmarks are Inception's own.

item.title: Viggle: JST-2 (physics-native world model)
item.description: Viggle's world foundation model represents scenes as persistent 3D "atoms" instead of pixels. Viggle says it generates an explorable 3D scene (decoded as Gaussian splats) in about one second at under $0.01 of inference, makes animation-ready 3D characters from a single image without separate rigging, and generates full-body motion from text or video. Up to 64 input views as spatial context. Available through Viggle's PINOC app and the Viggle API (100 free credits to start). Comparisons vs Meshy and Tripo are Viggle's own blind tests.

item.title: AWS: TorchNeuron: native PyTorch on Trainium (public beta, Apache 2.0)
item.description: An open-source native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium2 and Trainium3: existing PyTorch code runs with a device change ("neuron" instead of "cuda"), with eager mode, torch.compile, native distributed APIs and NKI custom kernels. Announced Oct 19; open-sourced under Apache 2.0 at github.com/aws-neuron/torch-neuronx and in public beta from Oct 20 (Neuron 2.33.0), timed to PyTorch Conference North America.

item.title: MiniMax: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
item.description: Next-gen Flash model for agentic tasks, coding, computer use and cybersecurity. MiniMax reports ~3× faster online inference and ~70% lower usage cost vs its predecessor; vendor scores include DeepSWE v1.1 73.7%, OSWorld V2 61.7 and CyberGym 82%. Flat API pricing $0.15 / $0.60 / $0.015 per 1M input / output / cached-input tokens; 1M context; multimodal. Was the anonymous Space Bunny Alpha on OpenRouter. Live on the MiniMax API, M Plan and MiniMax Code; open weights followed on Oct 23 (see that entry). Benchmarks are MiniMax's own.

item.title: VAST: EdenLive real-time generative renderer (open source)
item.description: Turns a game engine's rough reference video, a target first frame and a text prompt into detailed or stylized video in real time, while the engine keeps the game logic and world state. 5B and 14B weights plus streaming inference code and a WebRTC real-time service; VAST reports 24+ FPS at 720P, and the 5B model reaches ~24.7 FPS at 1280×704 on one RTX 5090 with LightX2V. Also ships a skill that turns a text prompt into a coarse playable game. Code is Apache 2.0; weights mix licenses and the first-frame workbench component is non-commercial. Release date per secondary coverage (Oct 18); link is the official repo.

item.title: DeepSeek: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (open weights, MIT) + Search & Fetch APIs
item.description: A minor update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with gains in reasoning, coding, agentic and visual benchmarks (DeepSeek reports DeepSWE v1.1 77.0, up from 74.2; Terminal-Bench 4.0 42.3, up from 31.2) plus shorter outputs and faster task runs. Live on DeepSeek's website, app and API under the same deepseek-flash name at unchanged prices; MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope. DeepSeek also opened its in-house Search & Fetch APIs to everyone at $0.75 per 1,000 calls per endpoint.

item.title: Perplexity: REA /reverse-engineer skill in Perplexity Computer
item.description: Computer can now use REA (Reverse Engineer Anything), morluto's open-source MIT-licensed toolkit, to inspect how an app works without its source code and then build a working version. Tasks that use /reverse-engineer are free through Oct 31, up to 10,000 credits per user. Announced on Perplexity's official Computer account on X.

item.title: Elorian: Glimpse (visual thinking model)
item.description: Elorian's first model reasons over images and video: tracking objects through motion, reasoning from other viewpoints and predicting physical consequences, with multimodal tools and subagents. Available today via API and Elorian's chat UI at $0.60 / $3.00 per 1M input/output tokens; benchmarks are Elorian's own.

item.title: NVIDIA: RTX Spark laptops go on sale
item.description: Windows laptops built on NVIDIA's RTX Spark superchip (Blackwell RTX GPU + Grace CPU) with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI compute, aimed at local AI models and agents, creative apps and gaming. Available from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, starting at $2,599; pricing varies by region.

item.title: Cline: Cline Cloud sessions (v4.1.25)
item.description: Cline can now run a task in a hosted sandbox on a GitHub repo and branch you pick; cloud tasks show in Recent and History, notify you when they finish, and keep running after you close your editor. Rolling out gradually.

item.title: Reflection: Beam 1.0 (open weights, Apache 2.0)
item.description: Reflection's first open-weight model: a 501B-total / 23B-active MoE with a 1M-token context, built for coding, reasoning and agentic work. Weights in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 on Hugging Face; also on Reflection's API and partners including Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter and OpenCode.

item.title: Kuaishou: Kling 4.0 video model
item.description: Kling AI's new-generation video model generates up to 30 seconds in a single pass, with steadier large-scale motion and complex camera work (tracking, orbit, push-in and pull-out shots) and up to 10-bit HDR output. Omni Reference combines up to 15 references in one task (up to 10 images, 5 videos and 7 subjects) and up to 10 keyframes; prompts can run to 8,000 tokens. Also reachable from AI agents through Kling MCP and CLI. Kuaishou says 4K, 1080p and 21:9 support, video extension up to two minutes and API access for enterprises and developers are coming.

item.title: Mistral: Timestral time-series forecasting models (open weights)
item.description: Mistral's first time-series foundation models, in 5M, 28M, 123M and 209M sizes, for zero-shot probabilistic forecasts (21 quantiles) over multivariate series with past-only and known-future covariates and up to 32,768 time steps of history. Runs efficiently on CPUs; Mistral says the 209M model ranks first on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench. Weights on Hugging Face under a Modified MIT license; code is Apache 2.0.

item.title: Liquid AI: d1-ultra (decision model)
item.description: Multimodal decision model that takes text and/or images plus yes/no, choice or score questions and returns calibrated probabilities in one forward pass (no output tokens). Available on the Liquid API at $0.042 per 1M input tokens; Liquid says it leads Artificial Analysis Decision Index by at least 8 points vs other decision models. Aimed at routing, moderation, inspection and agent guardrails rather than chat.

item.title: Perplexity: SPACE sandbox platform open-sourced (Apache 2.0)
item.description: SPACE, the sandbox platform that runs every Perplexity Computer session, is now open source: isolated Firecracker microVMs with pause/resume, snapshots, session branching, and network and credential controls kept outside the sandbox. Akamai, Crusoe and CoreWeave are offering or documenting deployments.

item.title: Black Forest Labs: FLUX 3 Image Klein (open weights)
item.description: A 5.6B-parameter open-weight image model for text-to-image, editing and multi-reference generation (up to 10 reference images), with native 4K output and bounding-box layout control. Weights on Hugging Face under the FLUX Kommunity License; also on the BFL API.

item.title: Krea: Krea 3
item.description: Krea's new image-editing model for production work: most edits return in under 8 seconds at native 2K, with characters and products kept consistent across references. Live on krea.ai and via fal, Replicate, OpenRouter, Together AI and others.

item.title: OpenAI: GPT-Live-1.1 (ChatGPT Voice)
item.description: Updated voice model for ChatGPT Voice with more natural accents and new voices in French, German, Hindi, Japanese, Korean and Mexican Spanish. Availability varies by region and account.

item.title: Meta: Muse Spark Open (open weights)
item.description: Meta's open-weight multimodal MoE: 816B total / 42B active parameters, 1M-token context, built for coding and agentic work. Weights on Hugging Face; runs locally on M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX, plus vLLM, SGLang and llama.cpp; hosted on OpenRouter, Groq, Together and others.

item.title: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt
item.description: Open models for agents: Super VL (120B) for servers, Bolt 74B-A9B sized for 24GB local machines with llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio and vLLM support. The 4GB Bolt E4B followed on Oct 23 (see that entry).

item.title: Anthropic: Code Review GA for Claude Team and Enterprise
item.description: Automated GitHub pull-request reviews leave research preview; most finish in 6-10 minutes, with Quick, Standard or Deep settings per repo. Eligible Enterprise orgs can claim credits through Jan 15, 2027.

item.title: Google: Deep Review (public release)
item.description: Agentic system that checks technical documents (papers, Docs, slides) for grounded, rigorous feedback. Two free reviews per week; heavier use via your Gemini API key.

item.title: Google: Gemini 4 Argon
item.description: Google's latest frontier model, aimed at hard coding, science and agentic work with a 1M-token limit. Available via API, Antigravity (Ultra), and the Gemini app (Ultra/Pro). Intro price $2/$10 per 1M tokens until Nov 30.

item.title: Noiz AI: Helix World (real-time audio-visual world model, preview)
item.description: Start from one image, move with WASD and look with the arrow keys: Helix World, from Noiz AI and HKUST, generates the explorable scene and camera-aligned stereo sound together at 24 fps on a single NVIDIA H800. Try it in the browser at helixworld.org; code (Apache 2.0) and a preview checkpoint are public, and local runs recommend an 80GB GPU. Benchmarks, including the new HelixBench, are Noiz's own.

item.title: Google Research: Harness² (open source, Apache 2.0)
item.description: Plug-and-play framework for recursively improving an agent's harness (prompts, tools, memory, skills, subagents, scripts, plugins) while keeping model weights fixed. Uses Propose–Probe–Compose without ground-truth verifiers; paper reports gains up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 on JobBench and 11.8 pp on LAB. Code on GitHub under Apache 2.0; paper arXiv:2610.14224.

item.title: Anthropic: Claude Haiku 5.5
item.description: Anthropic's cheapest, fastest small model. Sonnet 5.5 cache reads also halved in price, and Max/Team plans get monthly API credits.

item.title: OpenAI: GPT-6 with Intelligent UI in ChatGPT
item.description: GPT-6 Sol (paid) and Luna (Free/Go) arrive in ChatGPT Chat, answering with interactive UIs. Rollout to paid tiers started Oct 7, Free/Go the next day.

item.title: OpenAI: dots (cloud-computer agents)
item.description: Always-on personal agents rolling out in ChatGPT to Pro and Business Premium users in eligible markets.

item.title: Anthropic: Claude Opus 5.5
item.description: First of the Claude 5.5 family: long-running agentic coding and knowledge work, $4/$20 per 1M tokens, 1M context. Fast mode available in Claude Code.

item.title: xAI (SpaceXAI): Grok 4.7
item.description: Flagship for coding and knowledge work; 500k context, $2/$6 per 1M tokens on the API. Available in Cursor and Grok Build.

item.title: OpenAI: Agents API (public beta)
item.description: Brings the Codex harness and infrastructure to developers via API; pay only for tokens and tools used.

item.title: Meta: Muse personal agent
item.description: Meta's personal AI agent for everyday tasks, in a Muse app, WhatsApp and the web. Date per secondary coverage; link is AP News.
